title: How Much of the Person Is in the Policy? Measuring Interaction-Layer Commitments Across 245 National AI Policy Editions
content: Research comparing national artificial intelligence (AI) policy scores the state and its institutions, and rarely asks what a policy commits to where a person meets a system: whether someone subject to an automated decision can learn, correct, refuse or appeal it. We contribute Human-Centered AI Policy Instrument (HCAIPI), an instrument for reading policy at that layer, applied to 245 editions from 101 countries against twelve themes from human-computer interaction (HCI) research, recording how firmly each commitment is stated and whether anything would execute it. Of 13,587 relevant passages, 44.7% state a principle with no implementation detail and 11.4% specify a mechanism, a shape invariant to income band, length and volume. What a person is told or consulted about is instrumented at twice the rate of what they can do, and 65% of specified mechanisms are tasks for government. The lexicon recovers 13% to 54% of what a reader accepts; country figures track length.
